_about: Maps each Knowledge Base crop to the PIS commodity whose price should be used for its harvest estimate. conversion_factor turns Knowledge Base yield tonnes into tonnes of the product PIS prices. null means not sourced yet: do not show a naira value. Every row marked UNVERIFIED needs agronomist or PIS-team confirmation. 'reviewed-by-data' means the row only records that PIS has no series for that crop.
pis_source: https://pis-api.agrolinking.com/forecasts/{name} for the farm crops, and /commodities (document 'PIS prices for AgLens', 28 Oct 2026)

Market price, not a farm-gate price (PIS has no regular farm-gate source for this crop): a harvest valued with it is what it would fetch in a market. Beans (white) is dry white cowpea grain in NGN/kg (WFP shop price converted to wholesale); brown-seeded cowpea would use Beans (red). The yield is dry grain, so the factor is 1.0. This crop has no harvest estimate yet.

Knowledge Base yield is FRESH rhizome; PIS prices dried (split) ginger. The Knowledge Base's own ginger note says dried split ginger is roughly 20% of fresh weight, so 0.2 converts fresh tonnes to dried tonnes. Confirm the figure and that PIS is the dried price.

Market price, not a farm-gate price (PIS has no regular farm-gate source for this crop): a harvest valued with it is what it would fetch in a market. PIS prices SHELLED nuts per kg. Our yield is in-shell groundnut, so it must be multiplied by the shelling percentage (kernel weight divided by in-shell weight) before this price applies. No Nigerian shelling percentage has been sourced, so the factor stays null and no naira value is shown.
Yield is dry calyx and PIS prices dried calyx. A fresh-weight figure must never be used (fresh is about 10 times heavier).
Yield is grain tonnes and PIS prices grain per tonne. Use 'Maize (yellow)' when the cycle's variety is yellow.

Market price, not a farm-gate price (PIS has no regular farm-gate source for this crop): a harvest valued with it is what it would fetch in a market. PIS prices fresh pepper (tatashe) per kg; rodo and shombo are listed separately. Valid only because the yield is fresh weight.

Knowledge Base yield is paddy; PIS 'Rice (local)' is milled rice. A milling factor is needed and has not been sourced. Until then no naira value should be shown for rice. PIS confirmed on 28 Oct 2026 that Rice (local) is MILLED rice and that it has no paddy price (the daily rice exchange price is probably paddy but is not used: its source label changed and it moves 10 to 20 percent a day). Keep rice unvalued until a paddy price or a milling factor is sourced.
